blocks.content: INTRODUCTION TO MAGNETISM

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Like magnetic poles repel each other, while unlike magnetic poles attract.
An electromagnet is a temporary magnet produced by passing an electric current through a coil wrapped around a soft iron core.
Electric motors convert electrical energy into mechanical energy using the magnetic effect of electric current.
Electromagnetic induction, discovered by Michael Faraday, is the working principle behind electric generators.
The Earth behaves like a giant magnet with its magnetic south pole located near the geographic north pole.

blocks.content: Magnetism is a physical phenomenon by which certain materials attract or repel each other. A magnet is an object that produces a magnetic field and attracts magnetic substances like:
Magnetism plays an important role in daily life such as:
MAGNET
A magnet is a material that has the property of attracting iron and producing magnetic field. Magnets have two poles:
Important rule:
Like poles repel each other. Unlike poles attract each other.
PROPERTIES OF MAGNET

items: A magnet always has two poles.
Like poles repel, unlike poles attract.
Magnetic poles always exist in pairs.
Magnetic strength is strongest at poles.
A freely suspended magnet aligns itself in North-South direction.

blocks.content: TYPES OF MAGNETS
There are two main types of magnets:
MAGNETIC FIELD
Magnetic field is the region around a magnet where its magnetic force can be felt. Magnetic field lines:

items:
• Originate from North pole
  • End at South pole
  • Never intersect each other
  • Are crowded near the poles

blocks.content: EARTH AS A MAGNET
Earth behaves like a giant magnet.

items:
• Geographic north is near magnetic south
  • Geographic south is near magnetic north This is the reason why a compass works.
Geographic north is near magnetic south
Geographic south is near magnetic north This is the reason why a compass works.

blocks.content: Electromagnetic induction is the process of generating an electric current in a conductor by changing the magnetic field around it.
MAGNETIC COMPASS
A magnetic compass is an instrument used to find directions. It works on the principle that a freely suspended magnet aligns itself in North-South direction.
ELECTROMAGNETISM
Electromagnetism is the phenomenon where a magnetic field is produced due to electric current.
When current flows through a conductor, it behaves like a magnet.
ELECTROMAGNET
An electromagnet is a temporary magnet produced by passing electric current through a coil wound around a soft iron core.
Characteristics:

items:
• Strong magnetic field
  • Can be switched ON and OFF
  • Strength depends on current
Can be switched ON and OFF

blocks.content: USES OF ELECTROMAGNET

rows: Fixed and cannot be easily varied
Variable (depends on current strength and turns)
Fixed (North and South poles are permanent)

blocks.content: DIFFERENCE BETWEEN PERMANENT MAGNET AND ELECTROMAGNET
Permanent Magnet:

items:
• Permanent magnetism
  • Cannot be switched off
  • Weak magnetic field

blocks.content: Electromagnet:

items:
• Temporary magnet
  • Can be switched ON/OFF
  • Strong magnetic field

blocks.content: ELECTRIC MOTOR
An electric motor converts electrical energy into mechanical energy. Principle:
A current carrying conductor placed in a magnetic field experiences a force.
Uses:
ELECTROMAGNETIC INDUCTION
Electromagnetic induction is the phenomenon of production of electric current when magnetic flux linked with a conductor changes.
Discovered by Michael Faraday.
ELECTRIC GENERATOR
An electric generator converts mechanical energy into electrical energy. It works on the principle of electromagnetic induction.

items: Soft iron is preferred for making temporary electromagnets due to high permeability and low retentivity.
Steel is used for making permanent magnets because of its high retentivity and high coercivity.
Fleming's Left-Hand Rule determines the direction of force in Electric Motors, while Fleming's Right-Hand Rule applies to Electric Generators.

blocks.content: IMPORTANT SSC QUESTIONS
Q1. Who discovered electromagnetic induction? Ans: Michael Faraday
Q2. Which device converts electrical energy into mechanical energy? Ans: Electric motor
Q3. Which device converts mechanical energy into electrical energy? Ans: Generator
Q4. Which material is used in electromagnet? Ans: Soft iron
Q5. Which poles attract each other?
Ans: Unlike poles
